lesson.title: Comparing and Ordering
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 6, Session 4
lesson.footer: Fractions, Decimals and Percentages | Year 5/6 Maths | Session 4

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Years 5 and 6: comparing and ordering fractions, decimals and percentages by converting to one form and locating them on a number line
plan.shape: problem-first: students order a mixed set before the teacher models converting to one form, so the need to convert is felt
plan.criticalFeature: convert everything to the same form first, then compare
decisionPoints: the choice check: which is largest, 0.7, 3/5 or 65%?
the hinge: order four mixed amounts
plan.anchor: one amount, three names: fraction, decimal, percentage; make it out of 100 to switch
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 3? Show one amount three ways on a hundred grid (45/100, 0.45, 45%) before the launch.

studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The week's anchor on the board: one amount, three names: fraction, decimal, percentage; make it out of 100 to switch
A long number line from 0 to 1, marked in tenths

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Greater or less, ordering mixed sets, a mistake, and comparing sport results.
resources.title: Comparing and Ordering
resources.subtitle: Convert to the same form first, then compare.

items.prompt: Order each set from smallest to largest. Use = for amounts that are equal.
Ruby ordered these from smallest. Find her mistake and fix it.
items.answer: She ordered by the number of digits. 0.125 < 0.25 < 0.8, so the order is 0.125, 0.25, 0.8.

items.explain: 52% is 2% from 50%; 0.45 is 5% away and 3/5 = 60% is 10% away.

example.prompt: Ava scored 17/20. Ben scored 82%. Who did better?

items.prompt: Mia kicked 7 of 10 goals. Zac kicked 15 of 20. Who had the better goal-kicking accuracy?
Team A won 0.6 of its games, Team B won 13 of 20, Team C won 62%. Rank the teams from best to worst.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Numbers between two amounts, amounts greater than one, and a comparison game, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Between and Beyond
resources.subtitle: Find amounts in between. Go past one whole.

items.prompt: Is there always a number between two different decimals? Explain.
items.answer: Yes: add another decimal place, for example between 0.4 and 0.41 is 0.405.

items.prompt: Convert each to a percentage, then rank them from smallest (1) to largest (5).

example.prompt: Make a 'higher or lower' card game.
steps: Write 10 cards: fractions, decimals and percentages.
Turn one over; a partner guesses if the next is higher.

items.prompt: Write 10 cards for a higher-or-lower game, mixing fractions, decimals and percentages between 0 and 1. Then write the 10 cards in order as an answer list.
items.answer: Check: 10 different amounts in mixed forms, and a correct ordered answer list.

resources.description: For students who need more guidance: a conversion step for each one, then compare, with a hint on every question.
resources.title: Comparing: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Change them all to percentages first.

steps: Count the jumps from 0: each is 0.1.

items.prompt: Mark 0.2, 70% and 1/2 on the number line. Which is biggest?

slides.notes: Session 4 of our fractions, decimals and percentages week: today we compare and order all three.

Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk, and draw a long number line from 0 to 1 on the board. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Read a point
prompts: What are the coordinates of M?

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with coordinates and probability.
ASK: What are the coordinates of M?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (-3, 2)
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> say left or right, then up or down, from the origin. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's negative 3, 2: left 3 and up 2. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing (3, 2).
Fix: ask which side of the origin M is, and they add the sign.
notes.prep: Review of Week 2 coordinates (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Move a point
prompts: (2, 1) moves 5 left and 3 down. Where does it land?

beats: ASK: Where does 2, 1 land after 5 left and 3 down?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (-3, -2)
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> one move at a time, counting on the four-quadrant grid. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 2 take away 5 is negative 3,
and 1 take away 3 is negative 2. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing (7, 4).
Fix: ask which way left and down go, and they redo it.
notes.prep: Week 2 review: moving points across zero.

slides.title: Chance as a percentage
prompts: What is P(green) as a percentage?

beats: ASK: What is the probability of green, as a percentage?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 25%
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> count the equal parts, write the fraction,
then make it out of 100. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Green is 1 of 4 equal parts: 1/4,
which is 25 percent. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 1/3, from 3 colours.
Fix: count equal parts, not colours, and they recount.

beats: SAY: Now for our eight times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 8 times 3?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 24
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> double, double, double: 6, 12, 24. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 24. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 21 or 27.
Fix: double 3 three times: 6, 12, 24, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Here's the next one.
ASK: What is 8 times 11?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 88
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 8 tens, plus one more 8. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 88. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 81.
Fix: 8 tens is 80, plus one more 8, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: Now a division. How many eights make 72?
ASK: What is 72 divided by 8?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 9
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> count up in eights to 72. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 9. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 8.
Fix: check: 8 eights is 64, one more is 72, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to compare and order fractions, decimals and percentages.
successCriteria: I can place fractions, decimals and percentages on a number line.
I can order mixed amounts by changing them to the same form.
I can explain which form is easiest for comparing, and why.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: We know all three names now.
Today we put mixed amounts in order.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 the number line is reachable for everyone; SC2 ordering mixed amounts is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 choosing a form is the stretch.

beats: POINT to each amount.
SAY: Three amounts, three different names. Which do you think is the biggest?
ASK: Which is the biggest: 0.45, one half, or 48 percent?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 1/2
SCAN boards for 1/2.
80%+ -> cold call one student: How did you decide?
Less -> change each to a percentage together: 45, 50, 48. Re-ask.
SAY: One half is the biggest, at 50 percent.
It was hard to see until we changed
them all to the same name. That's today.
trap: choosing 48% because 48 is the biggest number.
Fix: change all three to percentages, and they choose again.
notes.prep: Problem-first: comparing mixed forms shows the need to convert. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: Equal in value, even if written differently.

beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is equivalent. Say it with me: e-quiv-a-lent.
SAY: Equivalent means the same value, even when it's written differently.
One half, 0.5 and 50 percent are all equivalent.
ASK: Are 0.3 and 3% equivalent? Thumbs up for yes, down for no.
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs down: 0.3 is 30%
trap: thumbs up for 0.3 and 3%.
Fix: shade both on a hundred grid, and they compare.
notes.prep: Equivalent is the idea that makes converting fair.

beats: POINT to the three amounts.
SAY: To put these in order, I change them all into the same form.
Percentages are easy to compare, so I'll use those.
MODEL converting.
SAY: 0.62 is 62 percent, and 3/5 is 60 percent.
So the order is 60, 62, 65: 3/5, 0.62, then 65 percent.
ASK: Order these from smallest: 0.73, 7/10, 76%.
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 70, 73 and 76 percent: 7/10, 0.73, then 76 percent.
trap: ordering by the digits as written.
Fix: write each as a percentage beside it, and they reorder.
notes.stretch: Would decimals have been easier here? Why?
notes.help: Write each amount as a percentage underneath it.
notes.prep: Convert to one form, then order: the critical feature. SC2.

beats: POINT along the number line.
SAY: This number line goes from 0 to 1,
and each jump is one tenth, or 10 percent.
MODEL placing 1/4 and 0.6.
SAY: A quarter is 0.25, so it sits halfway between 0.2 and 0.3.
0.6 is on the sixth mark. The further right, the bigger.
ASK: Which is furthest right: 0.85, 9/10 or 88%?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 9/10
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 9/10 is 0.9, or 90 percent, so it's furthest right and biggest.
trap: placing 1/4 at 0.4.
Fix: say a quarter is 25 hundredths, and they place it again.
notes.help: Count the jumps from 0 with your finger.
notes.prep: A number line shows order at a glance. SC1.

slides.title: Which is the largest?
slides.prompt: Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: thinks a larger denominator makes a larger fraction

beats: SAY: Change them all to the same form first.
ASK: Which is the largest: 0.7, 3/5 or 65 percent?
20 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to A
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: Why isn't it C?
Less -> write each as a percentage on the board: 70, 60, 65. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's A: 0.7 is 70 percent.
3/5 is 60 percent, and 65 percent sits between them.
trap: pointing to C.
Fix: write 0.7 as a percentage, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. C: 65 looks bigger than 7; B: fraction size misread.

slides.title: Order them
slides.ask: Write them in order from smallest to largest.
slides.pivot: change each to a percentage first, then order
slides.followUp: cold call one board: Which form did you change them into?

say: Write each set in order on your board.
trap: putting longer decimals last.
Fix: change each to a percentage, and they reorder.
notes.stretch: Add a fourth amount that goes in the middle of each set.
notes.help: Write each amount as a percentage underneath it first.
notes.prep: Guided practice including an equal pair and small amounts. SC2.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Convert, then order.
ASK: Write these in order from smallest to largest.
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> write each as a percentage: 45, 40, 42, 50. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 40, 42, 45 and 50 percent: 2/5,
42 percent, 0.45, 0.5. Tick it or fix it.
trap: putting 0.5 before 0.45.
Fix: write both as hundredths, 0.50 and 0.45, and they reorder.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone with 0.5 first or 2/5 last starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Compare and order fractions, decimals and percentages on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Which form did you change them into?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: comparing digits without converting.
Fix: change each to a percentage, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Extension: amounts in between, amounts over one, and a card game.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: a conversion step for each one, then compare.
notes.prep: Independent practice: greater or less, ordering, a mistake and sport comparisons. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Put the four amounts in order, smallest first.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: Can you put 0.3, one quarter, 28 percent and 0.32 in order, smallest first?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
RECORD who orders by the digits or misplaces 1/4.
They start tomorrow's check with the teacher.
trap: putting 0.3 before 28%.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: a new mixed set with a close pair.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner how you order mixed amounts.

notes.answer: open - listen for change them all to the same form, then order
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can order fractions, decimals and percentages?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with 0.3 before 28% matters most.
ASK: How do you put mixed amounts in order?
20 sec. Cue: Partner B first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: change them all to the same form, then order
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow: percentage of an amount.
